text.p: Following are the main stories in Monday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- National coalition chairman Mahathir Mohamad said all component parties should avoid taking political disputes to court but should instead solve their problems internally. He was commenting on infighting within the Gerakan party.

- Gerakan will consider adopting a rule similar to that in the United Malays National Organisation to automatically expel members who bring the party to court, Gerakan president Lim Keng Yaik said today.
- All states in Peninsular Malaysia have failed to gazette new forest reserves to replace those which they have converted to other land uses.

- More than 2,000 pensioners held a rally in Kuala Lumpur yesterday and passed four resolutions urging the government to give them a better deal. The group's resolutions include raising the minimum monthly pension to above the national poverty level and allowing representation on matters pertaining to pension payment and scheme.

- The construction industry's strong run may falter if measures are not taken to ensure sufficient supply of basic building materials, according to findings of a study prepared for the Ministry of Domestic Trade and Consumer Affairs.

- Today, for the first time, the Malaysian stock market opens itself to "shorties", the colloquialism for those who carry out short-selling, that is "...selling shares one does not own in anticipation of buying them back later at a lower price and profiting from the difference in price."

- With the outlook for both the Malaysian stock market and economy set to improve considerably by year-end, Malaysia will be an attractive choice for the astute investors wishing to bank in Asia, Jardine Fleming Pte's Singapore-based economist Rajeev Malik says.
